scenes.text: A chatbot answers one question at a time. [1] But an agent gets a goal, and works on it by itself, step after step. [2] So in this episode, let's understand AI agents.

An AI agent is basically an LLM, plus tools, running in a loop. [1] It plans the next step, uses a tool, looks at the result, and repeats that until the goal is done. So it [2] plans, [3] it uses tools, [4] and it checks its own results along the way.

data.definition: An LLM with tools, running in a loop until the goal is done.

scenes.text: Let's give an agent a real goal. Plan a weekend trip to Goa, for under fifteen thousand rupees. [1] Now it starts looping, plan, act, and observe. [2] First, it searches for trains. [3] Then it checks hotel prices. [4] It adds everything up, sees that it's over budget, and swaps the hotel. [5] And finally, it gives you a complete plan, under budget.

So what's the difference between a chatbot and an agent? [1] A chatbot gives you information, and then you do the work. [2] An agent actually does the work, across many steps and tools, and then reports back to you.

And agents are already here. [1] There are coding agents that write, test and fix code across a whole project. [2] Research agents that read dozens of pages, and write a report for you. [3] And customer service agents that can actually process your refund.

Here's a common myth. [1] People think agents are fully independent, so you can just let them run. [2] Be careful. Small mistakes can snowball over many steps. That's why good agents check with a human before important actions, like payments.

data.myth: Agents are fully autonomous. Just let them run.
data.fact: Mistakes can snowball across steps. Good agents check with a human before important actions.
